I'll think through this as the farmer would, then give the plan.

**My reasoning:**

I am 69. My wife and I work this land, 57 mu. It is big land for two old people but we have farmed this same ground for many years. For the busy times — planting, harvest — I pay the machine man to come with his tractor and combine. I cannot do it all by hand anymore.

Most of my land, about 50 mu, I do wheat then maize, wheat then maize, same as my father did, same as everyone in the village. On 7 mu of the good piece near the well I grow scallion — scallion brings cash money, wheat and maize just feed us and some to sell.

For wheat in autumn: I buy the compound fertilizer in 50-jin bags (the 15-15-15 kind, the blue bag). I put 2 bags per mu in the ground before plowing — that is what my neighbor Old Wang does and his wheat is always good. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I spread 1 bag of urea for every 2 mu — urea is cheap and makes the leaves dark. Three times water from the well: once before winter so it does not dry, once in spring greening, once when the head comes out. I spray two times — once for the yellow spots disease, once for the aphids. Seed I buy from the town dealer, the improved kind, about 30 jin per mu. Last year I got maybe 480 jin per mu, this year I hope the same.

For maize after wheat in June: no plow, just drop the seed with the machine into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed from the dealer — the local kind does not grow big ears anymore, everyone uses hybrid now. I put 1 bag of compound when planting, then 1 bag urea per mu when the maize is knee-high. Water two times if rain does not come enough. Spray for the borer worm once, maybe once for weeds. Last year 560 jin per mu.

For scallion on the 7 mu: scallion eats a lot of fertilizer, everyone says this. I put plenty of compound, and urea three-four times. Water often from the well — scallion likes water. Spray more because bugs love it. Price is uncertain but when it is good, one mu of scallion is worth five mu of maize.

I worry about fertilizer price going up again. But you cannot save on fertilizer — if you put little, the harvest is little. Better to spend the money and get the grain.
